slides.text: When my eccentric billionaire great-uncle Reginald passed away, the whole family gathered at the lawyer’s office expecting a bloodbath. Instead, the attorney wheeled in a brass cage containing Barnaby, an eighty-year-old African Grey parrot wearing a tiny velvet bow tie. 'The entire estate,' the lawyer read gravely, 'goes to whoever Barnaby names before sunset. Everything else is locked behind a voice-activated Swiss vault.'

My cousin Patricia immediately dropped to her knees, offering the bird Belgian chocolates and weeping about how much she loved wildlife. Barnaby tilted his head, cleared his throat in my great-uncle’s exact aristocratic baritone, and said, 'Patricia stole the silverware in 2014. Security, remove this peasant.' The room descended into chaos as six relatives tried bribing a two-pound bird with offshore real estate.

I didn't even try. I just sat in the corner eating a packet of salted pistachios from the lobby. Barnaby waddled to the edge of his perch, stared at my snack, and spoke directly into the lawyer’s recording microphone: 'I leave eighty million dollars to the quiet bloke with the nuts, provided he divorces his dreadful wife.' Anyway, I'm single now, and Barnaby and I are summering in Monaco.
